steps.title: Prepare microsome isolation buffers
steps.instruction: Make the following buffers using the listed final concentrations and quantities (per the indicated total volume).

substeps.instruction: Microsome isolation buffer liver (MIB‑L, up to 10 mL): D‑Mannitol 225 mM (0.41 g), D‑Sucrose 75 mM (0.26 g), EGTA 0.5 mM (0.05 mL of 100 mM, pH 8), Tris‑HCl 30 mM (0.3 mL of 1 M, pH 6.5), BSA 0.5 % (0.05 g), bring to 10 mL with MQ water.
Microsome isolation buffer cells (MIB‑C, up to 15 mL): Tris‑HCl 30 mM (450 µL of 1 M, pH 6.5), D‑Mannitol 225 mM (0.61 g), D‑Sucrose 75 mM (0.38 g), bring to 15 mL with MQ water.

Microsome isolation stability buffer (MIB‑S, up to 15 mL): D‑Sucrose 0.25 M (1.2 g), KCl 25 mM (0.028 g), HEPES 10 mM (150 µL of 1 M), EGTA 1 mM (150 µL of 100 mM, pH 8), bring to 15 mL with MQ water.
5× swelling buffer (SB, up to 15 mL): KCl 125 mM (0.14 g), HEPES 50 mM (750 µL of 1 M), EGTA 5 mM (150 µL of 100 mM, pH 8), bring to 15 mL with MQ water.
10× PBS (up to 5 L): NaCl 1.5 M (400 g), Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O 0.1 M (80 g), KH₂PO₄ 15 mM (10 g), KCl 25 mM (10 g), bring to 5 L with MQ water.

steps.title: Collect and rinse cells
steps.instruction: For each of five 150 mm dishes, aspirate the culture medium, add ~8 mL ice‑cold PBS 1×, swirl gently to cover the surface, aspirate PBS, then add 4.5 mL ice‑cold MIB‑S buffer. Keep all buffers on ice (≈4 °C).

substeps.instruction: Disinfect all work surfaces and equipment with 70 % ethanol before starting.
Maintain dishes not being processed in a 37 °C incubator (CO₂‑controlled if available).

steps.title: Scrape cells and pool suspension
steps.instruction: Using a manual scraper, scrape each dish in a single direction into the 4.5 mL MIB‑S already present; reuse the same buffer for all five dishes, accumulating the cells. Transfer the pooled suspension to a 15 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube (final volume ≈6–8 mL).

substeps.instruction: If trypsinisation is preferred, detach cells with trypsin, centrifuge, rinse pellet with PBS, and resuspend in 4.5 mL MIB‑S before pooling.

steps.title: Pellet cells (first low‑speed spin)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard the supernatant and keep the cell pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend in swelling buffer and incubate
steps.instruction: Measure the pellet volume (≈0.5 mL). Prepare three times that volume of 5× swelling buffer (SB). Resuspend the pellet in the calculated SB using a 1 mL Pasteur pipette. Incubate 35 min on ice (4 °C).

steps.title: Pellet swollen cells (second low‑speed spin)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 8 mL ice‑cold MIB‑S buffer.

steps.title: Homogenize cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the 8 mL suspension to a Dounce homogenizer (15 cm, tight pestle). Perform 20 strokes while simultaneously twisting the pestle, keeping the homogenizer on ice and avoiding bubble formation. Rinse the homogenizer with distilled and ultrapure water before use. Store 150 µL of the total homogenate at –20 °C as a control.

steps.title: Remove cell debris (first 600 × g spin)
steps.instruction: Transfer the total homogenate to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard the pellet; keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Further clean supernatant (second 600 × g spin)
steps.instruction: Move the supernatant to a new 15 mL tube and repeat centrifugation at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Keep the supernatant and discard the pellet.

steps.title: Isolate plasma membrane (1,200 × g)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant at 1,200 × g for 4 min (4 °C). The pellet is plasma membrane; resuspend it in 150 µL MIB‑C buffer and store at –20 °C. Transfer the remaining supernatant to an 8.9 mL ultracentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Isolate mitochondria and MAMs (7,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Using a Beckmann 90Ti fixed‑angle rotor, centrifuge the supernatant at 7,000 × g for 15 min (4 °C). Resuspend the pellet in 150 µL MIB‑C, store at –20 °C, and keep the supernatant in a new 8.9 mL ultracentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Collect plasma membrane contamination (20,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant at 20,000 × g for 35 min (4 °C). Resuspend the resulting pellet in 150 µL MIB‑C, store at –20 °C, and keep the supernatant for the next step.

steps.title: Isolate endoplasmic reticulum (100,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the final supernatant at 100,000 × g for 65 min (4 °C). Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the ER pellet in 150 µL MIB‑C. Store the ER fraction at –20 °C.

steps.title: Scale up for larger ER yield (optional)
steps.instruction: When more material is needed, process up to 10 dishes using the same 4.5 mL MIB‑S per set of five dishes (total 9 mL for ten dishes). Increase the resuspension volume in step “Resuspend in swelling buffer” from 8 mL to 16 mL. Use larger polypropylene tubes and split the final ultracentrifuge volume into two tubes, resuspending each pellet in 100 µL MIB‑C and pooling the two 100 µL aliquots. Typical yield is 250–300 µg ER per five dishes; to obtain ~1 mg, run the protocol on 20 dishes (four parallel preparations).

steps.title: Extract and wash mouse liver
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation, remove the liver whole, discard the gallbladder, and wash the organ twice in ice‑cold PBS. Wash a third time, then cut the liver into ~0.2 cm pieces.

steps.title: Homogenize liver tissue
steps.instruction: Place the liver pieces in a 15 mL glass/Teflon Potter Elvehjem homogenizer and add 4 mL MIB‑L per gram of liver (e.g., a 1.5 g liver requires ≈6 mL MIB‑L). Homogenize until a uniform suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Remove nuclei and debris (first 600 × g spin)
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL polypropylene tube and centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard the pellet (nuclei, unbroken cells, debris) and keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Second debris removal (second 600 × g spin)
steps.instruction: Move the supernatant to a new 15 mL tube and repeat centrifugation at 600 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard any lipid layer (thin white film) and the pellet; retain the clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Separate mitochondria/MAMs (9,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to an 8.9 mL ultracentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 9,000 × g for 10 min (Beckmann 90Ti rotor). The pellet (crude mitochondria/MAMs) can be saved; the supernatant proceeds to the next step.

steps.title: Pellet plasma membrane contaminants (20,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant at 20,000 × g for 30 min (4 °C). Discard any lipid layer that forms; the pellet contains plasma membrane and similar density membranes.

steps.title: Final ER isolation (100,000 × g)
steps.instruction: Transfer the resulting supernatant to a new 8.9 mL ultracentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 100,000 × g for 1 h (4 °C). Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the ER pellet in 500 µL MIB‑L. Store the enriched ER fraction at –20 °C.

description: Validation of protocol To achieve reproducibility, we fine-tuned the protocol by producing three replicates of our results. Additionally, three independent isolations on different days were performed to ensure the robustness of the protocol. The western blot analysis images presented previously in this protocol correspond to the optimal results achieved.
